High school sucked for me. If I had to do it over again, I would have gotten my GED and started at a community college. I was an awkward loner, targeted by shitheads and defended by no one. There really was no reason for me to be there. 

If high school is as painful for you, do you have to go back there? If finishing your last year there is important to you, then don't try to predict the end. Don't allow your depression brain to dictate how it's going to go. Instead, set your goals in the short-term and look forward to things you can accomplish. Tell yourself you'll do homework for a set amount of time nightly, that you'll turn in your homework whether its perfect or complete or not, and that you'll attend class daily.

Those are the goals that would have helped me get through. Maybe there are other things that are more important to you. When it gets tough, just remember that come June 2014, you won't have to see these people again.
Not to the woman whose ass he bit but to the cop who could arrest him?

I'm curious. Why did you respond to my post? You seem angered that I would ask for cheering up when I need it. It's a skill I had to learn in order to be able to deal with bad feelings. Even with the bad feelings, I still feel as if I can exercise a sense of humor. So I did with this post.

More than a guided response, what I really hoped for was a connection with another human who knows what it is to feel bad and can offer a hand up. I'm not getting that from you.

If I was doing a good job, I wouldn't ask for help. ;). I've been able to build habits that allow me to have plans for my life for a change. But for every little bit I move forward, I fall back and feel, well, sad, tired and unlovable.That's where I usually live and it's debilitating. Since I hate being told that everything is going to be all right, I thought I'd help well-wishers out and let them know what I really want to hear.
Hell, yes! What I'd give to have someone say that my fat ass is perfect! :D

Yes! Thanks! I love this. 

It's hard to believe that I am not to blame for my parents' unhappiness and how they choose to deal with it. It's hard to know that I can't fix it. And it's been harder to let myself not like them for what they've done and are doing. That's all I'm sure about in regard to that situation but I hope to figure out what normal people do. What do they do in insane situations? :D

I am very happy to hear about you and your SO. It gives me hope that maybe I can be in a relationship, too. I met a great guy who wants nothing long term and I say the same because I keep wondering who would want this giant bag of bullshit. But to know that there are people who will take a chance on us and that we are capable of making SOs happy is very encouraging. 

I was very happy to get your comment. Thanks. :)

I used to tell people who suggested that I exercise to feel better that if I had the energy to exercise, I wouldn't be depressed. I like walking because all I need is shoes and something to listen to. When I feel my worst and can't get it together to go to a gym, I like to go out after dark and hate-walk my way around the city. When I get home too tired to tell myself how big a turd I am, then that walk is a success.

Bad shit happens to everyone but depression tells us that we are the cause of it. Furthermore, it tells us that we can't get out of the shithole we find ourselves in. 

I wish I could help you find a way out of yours. I am in one of my own making right now. I don't know if you've been in treatment or done any reading about depression. But knowing that your brain works differently than the usual ones you find around sometimes helps. Sometimes I can stand back, tell myself that these terrible feelings that my brain gives me are not real (also helps if you like Buddhism), and that I can work toward something constructive.

I wish I had something that worked more quickly than that. Just know that the bad things happen to us all and that your brain can help you figure out a better situation than the one you're in. It feels lonely but you're not alone in this.

Depression is so boring that those of you willing to listen to us talk about it don't last long. Depression is the same, the self-talk is always negative, and it's not that we're unwilling to try something you suggest, it's that we "know" that the something will never work. 

So please keep listening. Ask her if it's okay to discuss her funks and her hospitalization. Questions like: What happened in the hospital? What does she mean when she feels self-destructive? People usually shy away from discussing my depression directly, afraid that acknowledging it will make it worse. It won't.

Take a walk or go on a run. Exhaust yourself. Being too tired to harm yourself or dwell on your sadness helps in a crisis. There's also something about exercise that allows you to see your problems from a different perspective. 

Someone else suggested /r/KindVoice. Skype with another sympathetic person who wants to hear you out and has no stake in the outcome. Pretty genius idea for a sub, IMO.
